problem.name: Fock-state boson sampling
problem.statement_latex: Given an $m\times m$ interferometer $U$ and single photons in $n\leq m$ specified inputs, sample $s\in\mathbb N^m$, $\sum_i s_i=n$, with $p(s)=|\operatorname{Per}(U_s)|^2/\prod_i s_i!$. Matrix $U_s$ uses occupied input columns and repeats row $i$ exactly $s_i$ times. Complexity uses optical operations and classical arithmetic time at specified precision.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(m^2)$ two-mode optical elements implement a general interferometer, followed by photon-number detection. Scattershot boson sampling varies the occupied input modes.
quantum.headline_text: $O(m^2)$ two-mode optical elements implement a general interferometer, followed by photon-number detection. Scattershot boson sampling varies the occupied input modes.

classical.headline_latex: Clifford--Clifford exact sampling costs $O(n2^n+mn^2)$. Their collision-aware algorithm has Haar-average bound $O(\frac{n(m+n)}m\frac{\binom{2m+n}{n+1}}{\binom{m+n}{n+1}}+n^2m)$. For fixed nonzero uniform loss, the November 2026 loss theorem gives polynomial approximate sampling with total-variation error averaged over Haar interferometers.
classical.headline_text: Clifford–Clifford exact sampling costs $O(n2^n+mn^2)$. Their collision-aware algorithm has Haar-average bound $O(\frac{n(m+n)}m\frac{\binom{2m+n}{n+1}}{\binom{m+n}{n+1}}+n^2m)$. For fixed nonzero uniform loss, the November 2026 loss theorem gives polynomial approximate sampling with total-variation error averaged over Haar interferometers.
